parsed.rationale: The pipeline reports a Jaccard similarity of 0.75 between `WXYCApp.navigateToPreviousTheme` (line 465) and `WXYCApp.navigateToNextTheme` (line 477), both in `WXYC/iOS/WXYCApp.swift` in package `app:iOS`. The high overlap strongly suggests the two methods share the same navigation logic and differ only in the direction of traversal. Neither record carries any restraint flag (`is_test`, `is_mock`, `is_sample_app`, `is_codegen` are all false), so the duplication is unintentional. Because both methods belong to the same type in the same file, the correct remedy is a shared private helper parameterised on direction rather than a cross-package extraction or a generic type.

specifics.proposed_action: Unify `WXYCApp.navigateToPreviousTheme` (line 465) and `WXYCApp.navigateToNextTheme` (line 477) in `WXYC/iOS/WXYCApp.swift` into a single private helper method — e.g., `navigateTheme(direction: ThemeNavigationDirection)` or `navigateTheme(offset: Int)` — where the direction/offset parameter encodes whether to step backward or forward. The two public call-sites become one-liners that pass `.previous`/`.next` (or `-1`/`+1`). This eliminates the near-duplicate body (Jaccard 0.75) while keeping the two descriptive entry-points if they are part of a public or @objc interface; otherwise the entry-points themselves can be collapsed.
specifics.why_no_category_fits: Both methods live in the same file and same type (`WXYCApp`), so 'extract-to-common' (cross-file/package extraction) is not the right frame. They are concrete methods, not protocol requirements, so 'default-implementation' and 'protocol-inheritance' do not apply. The duplication is a single varying axis (direction: previous vs. next), which is best expressed as a parameter rather than a type parameter, making 'generic-parameterization' a poor fit. No macro synthesis, subclass hierarchy, or PAT is involved. The most idiomatic Swift remedy is a shared private helper with a direction argument — a refactor that falls between 'extract-to-common' and 'generic-parameterization' and is most accurately described as a parameter-extraction / helper-consolidation.
